problems.source_says: Section 3.1 explicitly reports 247 as the final participant sample after seven removals from 254 enrolled adults. However, Section 3.6 also reports removing outliers and incomplete responses without counts or clarification that these are the same seven people. Section 4.1 repeatedly reports F(4, 237) for analyses described as one-way ANOVAs. With five groups, 247 observations would give 242 residual degrees of freedom; 237 residual degrees of freedom would instead imply 242 observations under that model. This is an inconsistency, not a verified alternative headcount: neither additional exclusions nor a reporting error can be established. The form already notes the conflict, but its definite n_analyzed of 247 remains unverified as the actual analysis sample; the exact analyzed count is unknown.
problems.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.1; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Sections 3.6 and 4.1. Markdown lines 93, 149 and 155.

problems.source_says: The five counts 50, 49, 49, 50 and 49 are explicitly participant counts in the Section 3.1 final-sample/random-assignment passage and sum to 247. They are not separately identified as the numbers retained in each analysis after the screening described in Section 3.6. No arm-specific exclusion counts or post-screening denominators are supplied, and the one-way ANOVA discrepancy prevents independently validating these as exact analyzed arm sizes. Figure 1 describes the procedure without participant-flow counts, and Table 1 contains moderator slopes, standard errors and p-values without sample sizes. The reported arm sample sizes are supported, but the exact analyzed arm sizes remain unknown.

summary: The exact analyzed total of 247 and arm counts of 50/49/49/50/49 cannot be fully verified because unquantified exclusions and inconsistent ANOVA degrees of freedom leave the analysis sample unresolved. The main randomized study still supports at least 50 analyzed people without adding the pilot or interview subset.
